item.title: Rockstar Games has confirmed GTA 6 retail sales reached $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, securing its place as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has confirmed GTA 6 retail sales reached $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, securing its place as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.
Parent company Take-Two Interactive announced the news today. Rockstar founder and president Sam Houser shared his feelings about the landmark achievement in a statement.
"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," he said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
After quickly emerging as the highest-rated video game of all time, breaking records across streaming sites, and causing wild spikes in internet traffic, we all kind of knew this was coming. After 13 years, Rockstar has pulled off the greatest score anyone has ever seen. Even in this new update, Take-Two said it was "proud" to help GTA 6 adopt its new crown.
Earning $3.79 billion in 24 hours is unheard of across any medium, meaning Rockstar's new Grand Theft Auto game didn't just stomp on launch sales for games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Cyberpunk 2077, or any Call of Duty game; it crushed any blockbuster movie release ever, too. It's still got a ways to go before claiming any titles like 'best all-time sales,' but it's a start better than anyone has ever seen in the history of gaming.
Just yesterday, it was reported that GTA 6 had managed to sell more than 20 million pre-order copies. Courtesy of Take-Two today, we now know that, somehow, these already staggering numbers actually significantly undershot the reality. The company has now confirmed that it actually moved 32.5 million pre-sale units alone. That's more copies than the vast majority of games have ever sold. Meanwhile, how many non-pre-ordered copies have been sold after launch is unclear.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. If this news is anything to go by, Rockstar is just getting started.

item.title: The next Baldur's Gate 3 prequel novel has been revealed, focusing on Shadowheart.
item.description:
Shadowheart is the next Baldur's Gate 3 character to get a prequel novel after "Astarion" by T. Kingfisher released earlier this year.
Published by Penguin Random House, Baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart, written by Tasha Suri, is already available for preorder at major retailers like Amazon. It will launch next year on June 8, 2027.
Here's the official blurb:
"A calculating priestess must investigate a brutal murder in this darkly fantasy from the World Fantasy Award winning author of the Burning Kingdoms trilogy.
Shar's blessings upon you.
Her name is Shadowheart. As a devotee of the dark goddess Shar, she knows little more about herself than this. But she does know faith and power, and what it takes to keep them.
In the end, all else is detail.
Beneath the bustling city of Baldur’s Gate and within the secretive, underground church she calls home, one’s past is a weakness best sacrificed to the fathomless Mirror of Loss. With oblivion comes strength, but without the bonds of memory, treachery festers among even the most ardent of Shar’s acolytes.
"When a member of their order is killed in the Upper City, Shadowheart and her so-called allies are called to investigate. She trusts none of them: not Mirie, the ambitious Griefguard; not Caldan, the cynical propagandist; and certainly not Nocturne, the charming quartermistress, who claims to have only Shadowheart’s best interests in mind.
But the wealthiest district of Baldur’s Gate has secrets of its own, and it hides temptations far greater than any Shadowheart remembers facing. Torn between the familiar comforts of the dark and the thrill of new desire, she must solve the mystery to prove her devotion… or be cast into the light."
Some fans r/BaldursGate3 had might already noticed there was a Shadowheart book in the works after several international Amazon stores posted a description for the now confirmed book.
But, excitement may be tepid from fans, since feedback for T. Kingfisher's Astarion prequel have been mixed. Fans have called out several retcons to the vampire's backstory, while also lamenting that the book "doesn't do justice to his character".
While Larian has left Baldur's Gate 3 and the Dungeons & Dragons universe behind to work on brand new games, including Divinity, it lives on. HBO is working on a Baldur’s Gate 3 TV show set after the video game, which not all fans are thrilled about.
Many can’t fathom why anyone would want to continue on from the events of Baldur’s Gate 3, given its many different endings, variances in world state, and, most importantly, the vastly different outcomes for beloved characters such as Astarion, Karlach, and Shadowheart.
Hasbro also plans for a video game follow-up to Baldur’s Gate 3, but whether that’s a Baldur’s Gate 4 that continues the story or something entirely different remains to be seen. In the meantime, these books will give fans something to chew on.
Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

item.title: GTA 6 players can't help but agree that controlling Jason's stash is harder than it needs to be, and they're asking Rockstar Games for a fix.
item.description:
GTA 6 players can't help but agree that controlling Jason's stash is harder than it needs to be, and they're asking Rockstar Games for a fix.
The newest Grand Theft Auto entry may have launched as the highest-rated video game of all time, but it isn't completely perfect. Leonida is a massive island with details tucked into every Vice City street corner, and early adopters are saying that one of its peskiest issues can be found without leaving Jason's seaside home.
You hardly need to get one hour into GTA 6's story to reach Jason's Stash, a secret collection of valuables tucked under the floorboards in his bedroom. For players, it's good for two things: keeping a box of cherished memories and stowing away piles of cash for safekeeping. The sad part is, doing that second thing is a major pain.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
It's a bit hard to explain if you've not played GTA 6, but if you have, you'll know what we're talking about. Depositing and withdrawing money into Jason's stash is finicky, to say the least. Controlling the amount means slowly counting by the individual dollar, and if you hold on the D-pad to input vastly higher or lower amounts of money, the count ramps up by the thousands in what feels like just a few moments.
It's the kind of flaw that couldn't possibly break the bank for a game swimming in ideas that have players thrilled, but when such a noticeable speed bump rears its head so early on, it means just about everyone who touches GTA 6 will encounter it. That's why it should come as no surprise to see so many people mentioning the annoyance online.
"The UI to pick how much money you want to deposit or withdraw from your stash or ATM. It's impossible to not overshoot the amount you are going for," one ResetEra user said. "Give me a simple +100/-100 set of buttons instead please."
"1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10,000," one Reddit user joked.
"Same," another said, "And man, what a f**king joy it is for this to be my biggest gripe."
It's hard not to laugh at such a minor inconvenience emerging as one of the bigger complaints in a game that has something for everyone. You can do everything from stealing cocaine from crashed boats to double fisting red delicious apples as you talk to your ex, so the fact that one of the only problems everyone can agree on is a small UI flaw stands as a testament to what Rockstar has created.
Still, players have found it to be pretty annoying. So much so, in fact, that some have refused to deal with Jason's Stash at all. Of course, if you've played GTA 6 enough, you'll know that, when you get 'Wasted,' you'll lose the money on your person. Hauling around thousands of dollars and engaging in a little road rage on the way to meet Lucia for a date can and has left players penniless.
"Yeah. I was like f**k this I'm just gonna carry my bankroll," one user admitted." Died for the first time immediately and lost it all lmao."
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
"Losing everything on death has pissed me off so bad already," another said. "You clip one driver at a red light, they get road rage and destroy the car and I lose thousands out of my stash."
"OK good, I'm not the only one," another player added. "Honestly the only thing I’m like 'can R* patch this?' I'm like 20..30…$2000 dammit!"
A stash is also inherently the kind of thing players will keep coming back to, meaning more encounters with that same blemish over time, which is why some are taking to online forums to voice their complaints. Rockstar will surely be busy patching other bugs and glitches in the near future, but fans hope Jason's Stash is high on the list for a fix.

item.title: GTA 6 has finally arrived after more than a decade of waiting, but apparently that's not enough for some people. Less than 24 hours after Rockstar's long-awaited sequel launched, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7.
item.description:
GTA 6 has finally arrived after more than a decade of waiting, but apparently that's not enough for some people. Less than 24 hours after Rockstar's long-awaited sequel launched, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7.
Appearing in an interview with TBPN yesterday, the day GTA 6 launched, Zelnick was congratulated on the game's success before being hit with a question that will haunt him for the decade.
"When do we get GTA 7?" one of the hosts asked, before quickly clarifying that he was joking.
"Once you get through several hundred hours of the most incredible fun you've ever had, ask the question again," Zelnick replied.
Fair enough. After all, GTA 6 has barely been out long enough for players to get properly acquainted with Jason and Lucia, let alone start thinking about what Rockstar might have planned for the next installment. But Zelnick wasn't quite finished being asked about GTA 7.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
Later in the interview, during a discussion about AI and how technology could allow developers to create increasingly ambitious games, one of the hosts suggested that GTA 7 could theoretically be a live recreation of the entire world. Zelnick, understandably, couldn't resist pointing out the absurdity of discussing the next GTA game on the very day its predecessor launched.
"Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 November 19th. Wait, let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19th. And you're asking a question about GTA 7."
The hosts joked that they were simply moving the goalposts, but Zelnick continued to marvel at the timing.
"My father-in-law had a line about whenever he had many great business achievements and a lot of admirers. And if he ever said anything nice, he'd say, 'Oh, those are yesterday's headlines.' But it's not even yesterday. It's today."
Of course, the GTA 7 questions were firmly tongue-in-cheek, and Zelnick didn't offer any indication of when, or even if, Rockstar might release another mainline Grand Theft Auto game.
Still, given that GTA 5 launched back in 2013, and fans have spent the intervening years desperately waiting for its successor, it's perhaps inevitable that people are already wondering just how long they'll have to wait for GTA 7. For now, though, Zelnick would probably appreciate it if everyone could at least finish GTA 6 first.

item.title: While we'll have to wait a little while longer for a PC version of GTA 6 that you can tweak to your heart's content, there are still some visual dials you can tune to get Vice City looking just a little bit better.
item.description:
While we'll have to wait a little while longer for a PC version of GTA 6 that you can tweak to your heart's content, there are still some visual dials you can tune to get Vice City looking just a little bit better.
There is a display page in the GTA 6 settings menu that you can get to by pausing the game and going to 'Settings.' Then, hit R1 (PS5) or RB (Xbox) until you get to the 'Display' tab. There are several options available, which are mostly aesthetic, but there are some things you can adjust, like Motion Blur, that can change the way the game feels.
The first couple options are Brightness Calibration and Safe Zone. For the former, adjust the brightness bar until the Rockstar logo is barely visible. I know it's tempting to crank the brightness to make it easier to see things in the environment, but with how much emphasis GTA 6 puts on immersion, it's really just best to follow the instructions here. Plus, I haven't really had any situations where the environment was too dark to see what I'm doing — not yet, at least.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
The Safe Zone setting just adjusts the borders of the screen. I'd leave this at its default setting unless there are parts of the game that are getting cropped out of the picture. Then, adjust using the D-pad untill all the white border icons are just visible on the corners of your display.
The next three settings — Player Status Effects Intensity, Hit Effects Intensity, and Awareness Effects Intensity — adjust the way that the screen effect alert you to what's going on with your character. I keep all of these maxed out because I like being able to react as quickly as possible. But if they're distracting for you, you can turn them as low as you'd like, just be warned: It'll probably make the game a little bit harder.
Then, there's motion blur. Full disclousure, I do not like motion blur at all, so I usually turn this down to 1 or 0. Basically what it does is introduce a blurring effect to your surroundings whenever you move the camera or your character quickly. Turn it up if you like it, turn it off if it gives you a headache.
The dismemberment toggle is pretty self-explanatory. Turning it on will show when limbs are taken off with certain types of injuries. Turn it off if it makes you queasy. The blood and gore intensity slider is a similar beast. By default it's set to high (3/3), but you can adjust it to either limit the amount of blood or turn it off altogether.
GTA 6 also lets you change the way that flashbangs affect your screen. You can either set it to bright, which will white-out your screen whenever you get flashbanged, or set it to dark, which will do the opposite. This is a godsend for playing at night, especially if you don't want to wake anyone up with a super bright flash on your TV.
Then there's brightness reduction. This might be the most impactful display setting for GTA 6, as it "applies a filter to the world that softens the output of bright lights without impacting the HUD." And while that might sound appealing for anyone with sensitive eyes, just be warned that it drastically changes the way the game looks. It ends up giving the world a washed out, almost blown out aesthetic that is decidedly less appealing to look at. Make sure it's turned off unless you're specifically looking to reduce the brightness of lights in the game. Luckily, the game will warn you when you toggle it on, and makes you confirm your choice before it actually goes into effect.
Finally there's high contrast shaders. This is actually an awesome accessiblity feature, and lets you assign high contrast shaders to the player, allies, enemies and interactive objects to make it easier to spot everything. GTA 6 is a visually busy game, and if you're visually impaired in any way, this can make the game a lot easier. The setting will turn on all the shaders by default, though you can toggle each of them individually. Players are yellow, allies are blue, enemies are red and interactive objects are gray. You can also change the fill opacity to make it less garish.

item.title: GTA 6's cops are meaner and easier to provoke than ever before, leading many players to obey the law and keep their head down early doors.
item.description:
Back in the day, the thing we were most looking forward to in any new Grand Theft Auto game was going on a big killing spree for absolutely no reason. I'm sure many of you were waiting to do this in GTA 6, making the most of all the new details Rockstar added to the long-awaited sequel.
However, now that GTA 6 is finally in our hands, there's a curious phenomenon throughout the player base: no one really wants to commit any crimes. Instead, it seems most of us are spending the early hours of the game going about our day-to-day lives while keeping our heads down. Some of us are even using turn signals when we're driving.
So, why are we playing GTA 6 so differently from the games that came before it? A likely theory is that crime just isn't worth the risk like it once was — the cops really mean business this time.
"2 hours in GTA 6 and I haven’t committed a single crime outside of missions," said X / Twitter user @BearsShowYo. "That new system got me spooked lmao," added @JuJu_Da_Gamer. "The cop system in GTA 6 is crazy lmao I’m genuinely scared to steal a random car," @OvOBrezzzy commented.
MDRRR, pitié j’ai jamais vu ça #GTA6 https://t.co/KnDd7rirJy
They're far from alone in this. "Went into someone's backyard, they threatened to call the police and I genuinely feared for my life man," said @NohanDGreece. "I jumped into the water to get away asap." "Have been a good boy so far, using my own car and minding my business, those MF are brutal," @hissdigg said. "I can’t go home because I’m wanted in my own neighborhood and I don’t have any money to change clothes," added @Adeux_ailes.
Worse yet, the cops have never been easier to set off. Some will even attack you for filming them arresting someone else.
NEW: GTA 6 cops DO NOT like it when you film them stealing money and brutalizing people during stops. https://t.co/Be7LxcHcF6
Because the cops pack so much of a punch this time around, it's completely changing how players interact with the game. "I was texting a friend a few hours into my playthrough that I was annoyed a taxi ride to my (Jason's) house was $162 because I didn't want to walk and she was like, 'Why tf can't you steal a car???'" said @BlueOwlzMedic. "It honestly didn't even occur to me."
"Out here stopping at red lights… cops got me committing no grand theft or auto," added @DallienceRNG.
The biggest change to how the cops work in GTA 6 is that they're a lot harder to shake off. It isn't just a case of outrunning them until they get bored; you've really got to put in the work to avoid getting busted.
First, you flee the scene. That gets them off your case for now, but they will still be hypervigilant in the area you committed the crime. So, you've also got to change vehicles, mix up your appearance, get a new disguise, and make sure you're not hanging out with the person you committed the crime with. Oh, and you better not be walking around while openly carrying a weapon, because that's a quick way to get them on your case as well.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
Another change is that there is now a 6-star wanted level in GTA 6. It's incredibly difficult to achieve, but if you can pull it off, you're in for a hell of a survival mode. And I really do mean survival mode, because it's impossible for the wanted level to decrease once you have six stars.

item.title: Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.
item.description:
Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.
Rather than the throat-shredding performance being something Bale had practiced beforehand, the American Psycho and Big Short star has admitted that he simply took a gamble on the voice while in the moment — and after beginning to feel self-conscious about how his natural tone sounded emanating from the Batsuit.
"Being in that suit, I just felt like it was really stupid just to talk normally," Bale explained while appearing on The Rich Eisen Show, adding that he had been given Val Kilmer's ill-fitting cast-off for purposes of the audition. Kilmer, of course, starred as Batman in the 1995 entry Batman Forver — meaning the costume was a decade old by the time Bale pulled it on.
The 10 Greatest Batman Costumes of All Time
"And so on the day I went 'ah, they're going to hate it but I'm going to go for it.' And I started doing this more bestial guttural voice. I went back home and showed my wife what I'd done and she said 'well, you've blown that one, haven't you?'"
On the contrary, however, Bale said he later discovered that "Chris Nolan... loved it," and the rest is history. Bale went on to be cast as Batman for the director's acclaimed Dark Knight trilogy. Nolan even added another husky mouthbreather for its third entry, as fellow British actor Tom Hardy left audiences looking for the subtitles during his scenes as Bane.
"I'm running around, a grown man dressed as a bat in rubber," Bale recalled of his audition. "I can't just talk like I'm hanging out. There's got be something deeper and darker and more monstrous to make this work."
In the years since, Bale's take on Batman's voice has become "iconic" — and that's according to Robert Pattinson, the current Bat, who told GQ that it had been "almost impossible" for him not to do similar when picking up the cowl, even though he had found it difficult to maintain during extended dialogue scenes. "It's so kind of iconic, the voice he was doing in it," Pattinson said. "[And] it's really, really hard."
Pattinson is next set to appear as the Dark Knight in the upcoming The Batman: Part 2, which will now launch in February 2028. While not confirmed, Pattinson's new commitment to James Bond could end his run as the DC Comics hero, meaning someone else will have to cough up their own take on Batman's voice in the not-too-distant future.

item.title: When army-sized battles rage in stuff like Game of Thrones, someone has to clean up the mess afterwards. That's the premise behind Battleground Cleaner Simulator, which tasks you with tidying up after chaotic medieval events like battlefields, drunken tavern brawls, and feasts that leave blood all over the castle, bodies with forks in their eyes, and so, so much more.
item.description:
When army-sized battles rage in stuff like Game of Thrones, someone has to clean up the mess afterwards. That's the premise behind Battleground Cleaner Simulator, which tasks you with tidying up after chaotic medieval events like battlefields, drunken tavern brawls, and feasts that leave blood all over the castle, bodies with forks in their eyes, and so, so much more.
Developed by Mad Muffin Studios and published by Garden of Dreams, Battleground Cleaner Simulator is a very unserious game in the best (and funniest) of ways, as you'll see when you take a look at the trailer above. You'll play as a lowly servant tasked with cleaning up the aftermath of various gone-too-far events in the times of knights and kings. You must scrub the blood off the walls, floors, and furniture, pick up and dispose of the bodies (some of which might have kitchen utensils jammed in their eye sockets), and generally just restore the place to being spotless – lest the ruling class get dissatisfied and decide to dispose of you too.
Battleground Cleaner Simulator - First Screenshots
"Work quietly, keep your mouth shut, and make sure everything looks as if nothing ever happened," Mad Muffin Studios describes. "Your clients are generous — but they don’t take kindly to loose tongues."
There's no release date for Battleground Cleaner Simulator just yet, so you might want to wishlist it on Steam to keep track of it as development progresses.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6's Bikini Girl has been found, and there's even a nod to the fan theory that she was Lucia all along.
item.description:
Rockstar snuck a reference to a popular fan theory into GTA 6, as you may recognise a familiar face during one of the early missions.
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
The Easter egg can be found during your first proper mission with Lucia, Day Release. Keep following the mission until you get to the yacht party, and then take some time to roam around and take in the sights. Go towards the back of the yacht, and you should come across a woman who will look very familiar if you were following the GTA 6 pre-release trailers: Bikini Girl.
Well, Bikini Girl is the name the community gave her, anyway. She made a brief appearance in GTA 6 Trailer 1, released back in 2023, and it sparked a bunch of fan theories that she was actually Lucia, just heavily customised. This trailer was our first (official) look at Lucia, after all, so it makes sense that fans were looking for any more clues about her identity.
However, it turns out we were dead wrong. During Day Release, you can come across Bikini Girl while playing as Lucia, making it clear they are absolutely different people.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
With that said, Rockstar appears to have put in a nod to the fact that so many of us thought she was Lucia. When you approach her, Lucia will have the option to say that the girl looks familiar. Bikini Girl will respond by saying that she's a famous model, and Lucia says this is likely where she's seen her before.
Indeed, Bikini Girl was quite famous in our world as soon as Trailer 1 dropped, so it's all very meta. The fact that Lucia is taken aback enough by her appearance to comment on it also seems to be a pretty clear reference to the theory that she was Lucia.
This is far from the only Easter egg players have stumbled across in GTA 6. As we reported yesterday, you can also find an apartment that is a clear reference to the show Dexter. Players have also found lore that strongly suggests GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption share the same universe.

item.title: Some GTA 6 players are refusing to make use of an infinite money glitch they say ruins the experience Rockstar set out to provide.
item.description:
Players have already found ways to farm infinite money, undermining the carefully paced economy of GTA 6 using multiple methods. While this happens with every game, it’s particularly strange here.
Why is it weird? GTA 6 already has infinite money. You can rob as many stores and businesses as you like and fence the goods, and while stores close down for a while after they’ve been robbed, they reset on a frequent basis.
You just have to play as intended, but some players are hellbent on farming cash in the most mind-numbing ways possible. The methods are all built around forcing the store closure timers to reset, so you can rob the same stores on repeat.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
First, they rob a bunch of stores and collect as much as possible, then they trigger a mission to start a cutscene. Once the cutscene begins, they restart the mission from the menu. When the cutscene begins again, they quit out of the mission, which forces all the stores to reset.
Honestly, it sounds arduous and you’d be better off exploring to find new robbery opportunities so you can experience fresh gameplay.
Another method sees players go to a lucrative building, get all of the money and narcotics from inside, and store them in the trunk of their car. Next they save the game and immediately load it up. The bags remain in your car, but the building’s loot resets, allowing you to rinse and repeat.
Most players agree that this is probably the worst way to experience GTA 6. “Nah I’m good! Didn’t wait 13 years just to glitch my way through the game,” said one fan.
“Takes away from the experience,” another poster agreed. “The games (sic) way too immersive to just skip the grind, takes the fun out of it.” Another said: “Nah I prefer to just, ya know, play the game and earn it.”
There are seemingly dozens of variations of this glitch, with the method slightly varying between them. In another, the player robs a different location and fences the goods before saving and reloading to reset the location’s loot.
Again, this genuinely seems like a miserable way to play the game — especially since more exciting and lucrative robbery opportunities open up as you progress through the story. It’s also probably just a matter of time until Rockstar patches it out.

item.title: Some GTA 6 players really want Jason and Lucia to be able to get as fat as CJ from GTA: San Andreas.
item.description:
Given all of the intricate details that have gone into GTA 6, it came as no surprise whatsoever to see body transformations return.
This means that Jason and Lucia's bodies will change based on how much exercise you're giving them and what you're feeding them. Like in Red Dead Redemption 2, this impacts your stats in combat, so it's well worth keeping an eye on your health app. (Check out IGN's guide, Fitness and Wellness Explained in GTA 6, for more.)
However, also much like with Red Dead Redemption 2, a lot of players were looking forward to getting Jason and Lucia as big as possible, purely for aesthetic reasons. More than a few of us had Jason dual-wielding cheeseburgers in Chapter 1 (yes, you can do that), to bulk him up as quickly as we can.
Now, the results are in, and some players were left feeling underwhelmed.
multiple of my mutuals just decided they won’t buy this game because she isn’t fat enough
@jsmekuro_ The funny thing is Max Weight Arthur in RDR2 looks beefier/fatter than Jason so he got a bit of a nerf there https://t.co/GqtdVrfjnW
@HeavyGungnir THERE IS NO FAT LUCIA MF HERE IS PROOF FROM MY PLAYTHROUGH THE MAX BODY FAT IS ONLY 142 YOU ALL GOT SCAMMED https://t.co/MUB52xDuhI
Fat Jason has his fans, but it looks like everyone is universally disappointed with fat Lucia capping at 142 pounds (about 10 stone, or 64.4kg). And even if fat Jason is bigger, he's got nothing on the Rockstar protagonists who came before him, like Arthur Morgan.
The saving grace here is that getting chubby in GTA 6 is a lot easier than it was in Red Dead Redemption 2. Fast food and junk food can be found down most streets in Leonida, right from the get go. There are no cooldowns on how much you can eat at home, either.
And yet, there's one Rockstar protagonist who has them all beat: CJ from GTA: San Andreas.
@SirJosephWindsr *laughs in fat CJ* https://t.co/Qg8pzAE7EP
There is already talk of modders rectifying all of this once GTA 6 is available on PC. I imagine it would be one of many, many cosmetic mods for the game once modders have it in their hands. What do you think of max weight Jason and Lucia? Would you have liked to see them able to get bigger? Let us know in the comments below!

item.title: Fortnite has added a series of secret GTA quests referencing GTA 4's Roman Bellic and the game's memorable "Cousin! We should hang out!" meme.
item.description:
Fortnite has added a series of secret GTA quests referencing GTA 4's Roman Bellic and his memorable "Cousin! We should hang out!" meme.
Epic Games' battle royale flipped the switch to activate the six secret quests yesterday, the official day of GTA 6's release, allowing players to receive a series of fresh tasks from Peely the banana in exchange for a whopping 120,000 XP.
These quests all reference GTA 4 — and Roman Bellic's frequent harassment of his cousin, protagonist Nico Bellic — by having Fortnite players pick up the phone to Peely, who requests they complete a nearby task. Fittingly, one of Peely's quests involves knocking over a set of bowling pins — a nod to how Roman would call to invite Nico to go bowling with him. "Cousin! We should hang out!" reads the quest's on-screen description.
Other quests direct players to encounter various existing Easter eggs present on Fortnite's current map, including hidden treasure caves, a Zelda-like statue puzzle, and a cute rubber duck race.
[GUIDE] Complete #Fortnite's Secret Peely Phone Call Quests, referencing GTA IV's Roman Bellic!- Hit the pins- Solve Puzzle of the Frogs- Start Duck Race- Find Cenote Treasure- Find Lighthouse Treasure- Find Super Secret Cave🎁 Reward: 120,000 XP⏰Ends Dec 5th, 4pm ET https://t.co/AikNexWas8
Fortnite is currently weathering the launch of GTA 6 fairly well, with player numbers for the game's main evergreen battle royale mode still in the millions despite Rockstar's masterpiece launching this week. Epic Games has done well to build up interest in Fortnite's current season by dangling the oppurtunity to unlock a fortnight of entirely free access to the game's lucrative item shop, something players are now grinding for in huge numbers.
As for GTA 6 itself, Rockstar is yet to reveal exactly how well the game has sold — though it's clear the game has been a huge success, just from the estimated 20 million pre-order copies that the game shifted before launch.

item.title: Let’s settle this once and for all. Can Jason and Lucia get naked in GTA 6?
item.description:
Let’s settle this once and for all. Can Jason and Lucia get naked in GTA 6?
Ever since the couple were revealed as the co-protagonists of GTA 6, it feels like that one question has been asked more than any other. Not, “How will the robbery gameplay systems work?” or, “Does the driving feel as exquisitely dangerous as it did in GTA 4?,” but instead, people just want to know how much skin will be on show.
Who am I to judge? Upon booting up GTA 6 for the first time, within its opening hours I’d already located one nudist bar and spent a little too long examining the variety of appendages on show. There’s no shortage of NPC nudity out there in Leonida. People walk along beaches, run out into the street, and sit by pools with no clothes covering their decency. But, how about Jason and Lucia?
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks, or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips. If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map.
Can Jason and Lucia get naked in GTA 6?
Showering can (and should, if you don’t want to stink) play a huge part in your daily routine in GTA 6. Not only does it boost your focus bar, but can have other gameplay ramifications, such as enemy humans and animals being able to pick up your scent more easily.
Of course, showering should be done with no clothes on — unless you’re playing the Japanese version of Grand Theft Auto 6, that is — and you can scrub up both Jason and Lucia from a camera view deliberately angled so you don’t get a good look around the front of them. I’m sure you’ve tried by now if you’re reading this, but no matter how forcefully you push that right stick, you’ll never get the angle you’re looking for. GTA 6 simply does not want you to see its lead character’s genitals. They bare their soul in their epic story, so this is the least grace we can give them.
Sex can play a big part in Jason and Lucia’s story if you choose to engage in it, though. Build a strong enough relationship between them, and you’ll occasionally get a prompt to engage in a spot of physical intimacy, whether that be in bed, in the shower, on the sofa, or other spots around the house. While, again, these scenes aren’t overly explicit with full frontal nudity never on show, both can be naked, with topless scenes not uncommon. If nipples are what you’re seeking, you shall find them.
So, can you see Jason and Lucia naked? Yes, and no. Intimate scenes often involve no clothes, but you’re never going to come close to watching a porn film here. That would just be odd.
The least you can ever walk around your home wearing is underwear, and if you try to leave the house, further clothes will be magically added to your character to spare their decency. Despite some wild and weird things available for you to find in GTA 6’s open world, it ultimately does want you to treat its leads as real humans, not complete freaks. Despite what some past leaks may have suggested, you can’t roam the streets of Vice City completely nude for all the world to see. You are, however, free to do that in real life, but you will likely end up in jail.
We have plenty more GTA 6 coverage for you at IGN, from letting you know how long the game takes to beat to the optional missions you really shouldn’t miss.

item.title: GTA 6's full credits have sparked a rumor about a returning character. Are they really in the game?
item.description:
Warning! This article contains a major spoiler for the GTA 6 story.
GTA 6 is finally here, and players are already devouring it, finding each and every one of its secrets and surprises at a rapid pace. We have no doubt that some are so well-hidden that we won’t discover them for weeks, months, or even years, but when it comes to others, the cat is firmly out of the bag.

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks, or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips. If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Why is everyone suddenly talking about Niko Bellic in GTA 6?
Well, yesterday, developer Rockstar finally revealed the GTA 6 credits. Within that long, long webpage is the full cast of actors and the characters they play in the game. One name was snuck in right at the bottom, though. One that would mean a lot to long-term fans of the series: Michael Hollick.
Hollick, for those not well-versed in GTA’s past, voiced the Grand Theft Auto 4 protagonist, Niko Bellic. So, assumptions have been made that the beloved character may well make an appearance in GTA 6. In the credits, the actor is listed as playing someone simply listed as ‘The Hitman.’ The burning question is: Does Niko Bellic have a cameo, or maybe even a larger role in Jason and Lucia’s story, or is this mystery hitman an original character?
Really, do not read past this point if you don’t want any late-game spoilers for GTA 6. While I will not go into what it means for Jason and Lucia’s story, I will be talking about a major surprise you might want to experience yourself. You have been warned.
Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6?
Yes, ‘The Hitman’ is indeed Niko Bellic. That pseudonym makes a lot of sense — he spends much of his time in GTA 4’s story as a gun for hire, bringing his military experience in the Yugoslav Wars to the streets of Liberty City. And from the looks of him here and the situation we find him in, not a whole lot has changed in the intervening 18 years.
Niko is still heavily involved in the criminal underworld, albeit just dealing with his business with a few extra grey hairs these days, and has been called to Vice City to help eradicate a problem for the people he’s working for. I won’t go into what this means for GTA 6’s tale or how Jason and Lucia find their story connecting to another of the series’ protagonists, but I will confirm that it's all highly enjoyable for the short time we get to meet Mr Bellic again. Sadly, that doesn’t involve going bowling with his cousin.
GTA 4 and Niko are incredibly beloved at this point, with people often citing him as the strongest Grand Theft Auto protagonist to this day. It was a turning point for a more mature era of Rockstar storytelling, ultimately leading to the more empathetic nature of GTA 6’s story. Only time will tell if either Jason or Lucia will be held in such regard as 2008’s Liberty City immigrant with a dream, as more and more people finish their story.
That being said, if you’re someone reading this who has either finished GTA 6, or isn’t fussed about cameo spoilers, please don’t share this with others who you know won’t want to know this information. GTA 6 is a special game, so letting others enjoy it at their own pace with all its secrets and surprises still held up its sleeve is the kindest thing you could do.

item.title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey sparked a fresh surge in back-catalog sales for 2018's Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Ubisoft has said.
item.description:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey sparked a fresh surge in back-catalog sales for 2018's Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Ubisoft has said.
In its latest financial results briefing, the Assassin's Creed publisher noted how a "major summer movie" had "materially benefited" the continued sales of its brilliant Ancient Greek game. Over the summer, Ubisoft re-promoted Assassin's Creed Odyssey alongside the launch of Nolan's film, inviting players to go start their own epic journey for themselves after returning home from theaters.
Once again, Ubisoft used its financial update to praise the evergreen sales of its Assassin's Creed back catalog. Also, once again, it failed to provide any further detail on how last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows had fared. There's a sense that the long-awaited feudal Japan blockbuster has been a commercial disappointment for Ubisoft, and it's been a while since we had any formal update on sales numbers. No further content for the game is on the way, either — even though 2020's Valhalla just got a New Game Plus mode.
The Odyssey Cast and Characters: Who's Who in the Christopher Nolan Film
Indeed, Shadows is not mentioned at all in the results, despite Ubisoft commenting on Odyssey, Valhalla (which also just passed 40 million players), and this year's Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced — the latter of which has clearly had a successful launch.
Ubisoft attributes an outperformance in its latest financial results to Resynced, which it describes as having been "among the industry's most successful Action-Adventure remakes." How did its launch compare to any all-new Assassin's Creed games? If it did surpass any of those, Ubisoft perhaps understandably isn't saying — but it's clear the game has been a hit.
"The franchise will celebrate its 20th anniversary next year," Ubisoft said, reiterating what fans have heard already — that 2027 should be a more exciting year for the series than the past 12 months have been. "This is a major milestone for the brand, which is preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and communitymoments."
It seems likely that next year will be when we get a first glimpse of the upcoming Assassin's Creed Hexe, the series' next blockbuster game, as well as Netflix's upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series set in Ancient Rome and a peek at Codename Invictus, a new multiplayer game spinoff. Until then, well, Assassin's Creed: Odyssey is really worth a go if you haven't played it already.

item.title: Players have found lore in GTA 6 that strongly suggest the game takes place in the same universe as Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption series, in a move that has excited fans about the prospect of a canon merger of timelines.
item.description:
Players have found lore in GTA 6 that strongly suggest the game takes place in the same universe as Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption series, in a move that has excited fans about the prospect of a canon merger of timelines.
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 follow.
We’ve already found Arthur Morgan’s hat in GTA 6, but there’s another thing connecting the two games. A readable book found in Brian’s Marina in Key Lento has multiple references to Red Dead Redemption and its sequel. X / Twitter user GameRoll shared excerpts from the book online. The book is a chronicle of the life and death of Flaco Hernandez, a gunslinger Arthur Morgan hunts to his cabin by Cairn Lake in Grizzlies West during the The Noblest of Men, and a Woman stranger mission in RDR 2. The book itself could even be the chronicle you help Theodore Levin write by hunting down the gunslingers, or at least a modern reinterpretation of it.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
It’s told from the viewpoint of Rust McCreary, an original character who doesn’t appear in either RDR game. In the book, he comes across the corpse of Hernandez in the snow at Cairn Lake, right where you leave him in the RDR 2 mission.
According to the book, Hernandez had a bullet hole right in the center of his forehead, so it’s canon that you can actually aim good. The book also references multiple locations, from New Austin to Armadillo and Blackwater.
It’s not quite confirmation that Jason is a direct descendant of Arthur Morgan or anything like that, but it’s a cool detail that basically turns RDR into a prequel to GTA 4 and its sequels. Like Dutch, Rockstar had a plan all along. Players have even found license plates for New Austin in GTA 6. New Austin is one of the states in which Red Dead takes place, and is assumed to be Rockstar's version of Texas.
It's not the first time Rockstar has connected the games. In the first iteration of GTA Online, the character creator allowed you to share genetics with John Marston, protagonist of the first RDR, to create a visual basis for your original character. Fans of the two games are generally happy with the connection. "Honestly? Good," said one X / Twitter user. "I was annoyed that technically both canons weren't linked. By linking them, it makes the universe feel bigger."
"That is so cool," said another. "This GTA trully feels like RDR. And I really enjoy the calmer aproach I even try to be as good with jason to give them the better possible ending." Another social media user wasn't as convinced because of characters in older Rockstar games mentioning California and Florida, instead of their in-universe names of San Andreas and Leonida: "It’s weird though, because in Red Dead Redemption 2 they call certain states or cities by their real names, but in GTA they use fictionalized names of cities and states. So many retcons it’s painful."

item.title: Rosario Dawson has shared the first look at her return as Claire Temple in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, marking her long-awaited comeback to the MCU.
item.description:
Rosario Dawson has shared the first look at her return as Claire Temple in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, marking her long-awaited comeback to the MCU.
Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow...
Posting on Instagram, Dawson revealed a photo of her in costume for her first Marvel appearance in a decade, standing in nurse scrubs next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It's a scene that fans thought they'd never get to see, after it was deleted from the final cut of the movie, disappointing those waiting for Dawson's reappearance.
Now, however, it is being reinstated for the film's extended edition re-release, entitled Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day, alongside a handful of other moments previously left on the cutting room floor.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day - Our Biggest Burning Questions
"It's a brand new BRAND NEW DAY with our friendly neighborhood Spider-Man...!" Dawson wrote. "So excited to enjoy this record-breaking movie on the big screen (starting on December 4th) with an extended cut of new scenes and surprises… Ahhhh!
"Join me in getting tickets NOW!!!" Dawson continued. "PS: mom can finally share her bts photos❣️"
It's pretty obvious when this scene will take place, as Dawson's character stands next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man who is wearing a hospital gown and his Spidey mask. Of course, Spider-Man finds himself in hospital towards the end of the movie, and Dawson's return will likely answer fan questions surrounding how the superhero got patched up with no one else discovering his identity. (The answer, surely, is that Dawson takes care of him directly — having been used to keeping numerous superhero identities secret in the past.)
Debuting in the very first season of Daredevil back in 2015, Dawson’s no-nonsense nurse quickly became an indispensable ally across its sister Netflix shows: Jessica Jones, Luke Cage, Iron Fist, and The Defenders. Whether she was patching up Matt Murdock in a dimly lit apartment, helping Luke Cage navigate Harlem, or standing her ground against The Hand, Claire earned a fan following for her work sewing up the wounds of New York's vigilante community.
However, after her appearance in the second season of Luke Cage in 2018, Dawson stepped away from the role, leaving fans wondering for years whether Claire Temple would ever cross paths with the broader MCU. With Charlie Cox’s Matt Murdock and Jon Bernthal’s Frank Castle re-entering the fold, Dawson’s return felt like a missing puzzle piece — and Spider-Man: Brand New Day is finally delivering on that promise.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day will be back in theaters on December 4, 2026, now with Rosario Dawson included. What else has Marvel added back into the movie? You'll just have to go along and find out.

item.title: Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days.
item.description:
Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days.
It was thought that the person or group responsible for the online Cyberleek persona had ended their spate of GTA 6 leaks last month, after their memecoin crashed despite efforts to boost its market cap.
In October, Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, and threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap. Gameplay clips reportedly leaked at the time allegedly showed Lucia fully naked — something that is not possible in the final launch version of the game.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Yesterday, November 19 — the GTA 6 release date — Cyberleek returned to drop a GTA 6 Xbox build without the game's executable. In a statement reportedly published online, Cyberleek claimed this Xbox build is a “full November 2026 build of GTA 6.” They predicted this Xbox build would be used to emulate GTA 6 on PC “within a week, running far past 30fps.”
The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.
Cyberleek has revived their crypto scheme, promising to release the executable immediately if it hits a $15 million market cap. While the CyberLeek memecoin was boosted in value by the news to $1.9 million yesterday, it is unlikely to get anywhere near the target.
Still, Cyberleek has vowed to release the final file anyway on November 23, whether the memecoin hits the market cap or not.
The release of a full and recent build of GTA 6 would of course be hugely damaging for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, which appears to have been unable to deter Cyberleek’s actions in any meaningful way since their spate of leaks began.
It would also run counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch.
Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.
IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked. A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.
Cyberleek had threatened Rockstar and Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they failed to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of the memecoin hit $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam.
Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.
Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

item.title: Lanterns star Aaron Pierre had already reprised his role as Green Lantern John Stewart for the 2027 film Man of Tomorrow when the news broke that DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran had been fired by new parent company Skydance. Whether his appearance will remain in the final film now that there’s a new regime in charge of DC, Pierre says, “I’m very at peace. What will be will be.”
item.description:
Lanterns star Aaron Pierre had already reprised his role as Green Lantern John Stewart for the 2027 film Man of Tomorrow when the news broke that DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran had been fired by new parent company Skydance. Whether his appearance will remain in the final film now that there’s a new regime in charge of DC, Pierre says, “I’m very at peace. What will be will be.”
In a podcast chat with IndieWire recorded the same day the news about Gunn and Safran broke, Pierre says, “Well, I actually only just found out the news prior to logging on so I haven’t very much time at all to process the enormity of that news. But what I can say is that my relationship with James and my relationship with Peter is a beautiful relationship and I’ve really loved every moment collaborating with them and working with them and getting to know them. And I’m excited to, beyond this point, in a different context, collaborate with them again and I’m also excited to see what happens next for DC.”
The Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow was in post-production when Gunn and Safran were removed from their posts. It didn’t take long for the online rumor mill to flood the internet with claims that Skydance was going to remove many of the cameos from Man of Tomorrow, namely Supergirl and Blue Beetle. John Stewart is among the DC heroes set to appear in the film.
Gunn, though, shot down all such claims of studio meddling, stating that no one at Skydance has even seen the film yet. "There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made," Gunn posted. "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie - the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false."
It remains unclear what DC Studios’ future looks like until Jeremy Latcham, the incoming President and Chief Creative Officer of DC Studios, takes his post on December 1. For his part, Pierre is remaining zen about what’s in store for Man of Tomorrow and DC’s future. (The status of Lanterns Season 2 also remains up in the air.)
DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show
“I think for me, you know, we did the film and we really loved every moment of doing the film and what happens beyond this point is not my decision. So I’m very at peace,” Pierre tells IndieWire.
“What will be will be. But what I do know is that those friendships will last beyond this point and also those artistic creative, working collaboration relationships will live beyond this point as well. And as I say, I’m excited to see where DC goes from here.”
Until Latcham says otherwise, fans can only suspect things are back to square one again lest they heed some fans’ advice not to reboot the DCU again. If that’s it for Gunn and Safran’s “Gods and Monsters” saga then why should fans be invested in Man of Tomorrow if it no longer matters? It will likely just collapse at the box office like The Flash did after Gunn ended the DCEU.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.
